rows.basis: Both are the transition plan for climate change mitigation, covering decarbonisation levers, targets, investments, locked-in emissions, board approval and progress. Content directly corresponds.
Both require disclosure of climate change mitigation and adaptation policies per MDR-P/GDR-P. Same subject despite number shift.
Both cover actions and resources for climate mitigation/adaptation, presenting actions by decarbonisation lever and achieved/expected GHG reductions.
Both are climate-related targets, requiring GHG emission reduction targets for scopes 1/2/3, science-based/1.5°C statement, and target scope reconciliation with inventory.
Both disclose total energy consumption and mix in MWh disaggregated by fossil, nuclear, renewable sources, with high climate impact sector breakdown.
Both require gross scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions in tCO2eq, EU ETS percentage, location/market-based scope 2, significant scope 3 categories, and consolidation disaggregation.
Both cover GHG removals and storage from projects plus carbon credits from projects outside the value chain, and GHG neutrality claims using carbon credits.
Both are internal carbon pricing, disclosing scheme type, application in decision-making, and carbon prices applied.
Both disclose anticipated financial effects from material physical and transition risks and climate-related opportunities, including assets/net revenue at risk and stranded assets.

Identification of climate-related risks and scenario analysis (classifying physical vs transition risks, exposure/sensitivity methodology, scenario ranges) has no counterpart among the 2025 E1 DRs, which located this content in ESRS 2 SBM/IRO.
Resilience of strategy and business model to climate-related risks is a standalone 2026 DR; the 2025 E1 set had no dedicated resilience DR (it lived in ESRS 2 SBM-3).
Both require disclosure of pollution-related policies; the 2026 version condenses this into a reference to ESRS 2 GDR-P but the requirement content is the same.
Both cover pollution-related actions and resources allocated to their implementation, the 2026 version referencing ESRS 2 GDR-A.
Both require disclosure of pollution-related targets, the 2026 version referencing ESRS 2 GDR-T.

Both require disclosure of amounts of pollutants emitted to air, water and soil from own operations plus microplastics generated/used, though the 2026 version narrows to material emissions and primary microplastics.
Both cover substances of concern and substances of very high concern (production, use, import/export, release), with the 2026 version restructuring by manufacturer/user/article roles.
The 2025 DR on anticipated financial effects from pollution-related risks and opportunities has no counterpart in the 2026 DRs, which end at E2-5 on substances.

Both require disclosure of water-related policies and both address the case of sites in water-stressed areas not covered by a policy. The 2026 version drops the marine-resources scope but the core policy requirement matches.
Both require disclosure of water-related actions and resources allocated to their implementation, and both specify actions in areas of water stress/risk.
Both require disclosure of water-related targets, with reference to areas of water stress/risk.

Both cover quantitative water metrics for own operations — total water consumption, consumption in water-stressed areas, recycled/reused, and stored water. The 2026 version adds withdrawal and discharge metrics.

The 2025 DR on anticipated financial effects from water and marine resources risks and opportunities has no counterpart in the 2026 revised DRs, which contain only policies, actions, targets and metrics.

Both concern the biodiversity and ecosystems transition plan and its alignment with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, though the 2026 version is heavily condensed to just disclosing key features of any existing plan.

Both require disclosure of biodiversity/ecosystems policies including traceability of products/raw materials and sites in/near biodiversity-sensitive areas, plus sustainable land/ocean/deforestation practices.
Both cover biodiversity actions and resources allocated, specifically disclosing biodiversity offsets (aim, financing effects, area, type, quality criteria, standards).
Both cover biodiversity/ecosystems targets and the use of biodiversity offsets in setting targets; 2026 version condensed but same subject.
Both report metrics on material impacts on biodiversity/ecosystems change, including sites in/near biodiversity-sensitive areas and drivers/state of species/ecosystems.
The 2025 DR on anticipated financial effects from biodiversity risks and opportunities has no counterpart among the 2026 DRs, which end at metrics (E4-5).
Both describe policies for managing resource use and circular economy impacts, risks and opportunities; new version references GDR-P and eco-design/circular principles integration.
Both cover resource use and circular economy actions and resources; new version simplified to reference GDR-A.
Both address resource use and circular economy targets; new version streamlined to reference GDR-T.
Both are Resource inflows disclosures covering materials used, critical raw materials and secondary/recycled resources with weights and percentages.
Both are Resource outflows disclosures covering product durability, repairability, recyclability and detailed waste generation/diversion/disposal breakdowns including radioactive waste.
The 2025 DR on anticipated financial effects from resource use and circular economy risks/opportunities has no counterpart in the 2026 revised standard, which ends at Resource outflows.

old_dr_titles: Transition plan for climate change mitigation
new_dr_titles: Transition plan for climate change mitigation
rows.change_description: Same transition-plan requirement, but the ten sub-points of para 16 are consolidated into five key-feature items (para 12). The EU Paris-aligned Benchmark exclusion (16(g)) and the Taxonomy-alignment objective (16(e)) are dropped, and a new disclosure on key assumptions and dependencies (12(c)) is added, so what must be disclosed changed materially.

old_dr_titles: Policies related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
new_dr_titles: Policies related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
rows.change_description: Same subject (climate change mitigation/adaptation policies) but heavily streamlined: the explicit list of policy areas to address (mitigation, adaptation, energy efficiency, renewable energy, other) in para 25 is removed and the requirement now simply points to ESRS 2 GDR-P. DR number shifts from E1-2 to E1-4.

old_dr_titles: Actions and resources in relation to climate change policies
new_dr_titles: Actions and resources in relation to climate change mitigation and adaptation
rows.change_description: Same actions-and-resources requirement, presenting mitigation actions by decarbonisation lever and achieved/expected GHG reductions. The detailed CapEx/OpEx linkage to financial statements and taxonomy KPIs (para 29(c)) is removed, and the expected GHG reduction is now itself broken down by decarbonisation lever.

old_dr_titles: Targets related to climate change mitigation and adaptation
new_dr_titles: Targets related to climate change
rows.change_description: The climate-targets requirement is retained but streamlined into E1-6: GHG reduction targets for scopes 1/2/3, the science-based/1.5°C statement and the scope-vs-inventory reconciliation remain, while the mandatory 2030/2050 target-year values (para 34(d)) and five-year base-year update rules (34(c)) are dropped. The deterministic proposal's extra candidates E1-4 (policies) and E1-5 (actions) do not correspond to this targets DR.
rows.divergence_note: The authoritative text shows the targets DR maps uniquely to new E1-6 (GHG reduction targets); the deterministic candidate additionally listed E1-4 (policies) and E1-5 (actions), which cover different subject matter and were removed.

old_dr_titles: Energy consumption and mix
new_dr_titles: Energy consumption and mix
rows.change_description: Core energy consumption and mix disclosure (fossil/nuclear/renewable, high-climate-impact-sector fossil breakdown, energy production) is retained. The renewable-source sub-breakdown (para 37(c) i-iii) is simplified to a single line, and the entire 'Energy intensity based on net revenue' block (paras 40-43) is deleted.

old_dr_titles: Gross Scopes 1, 2, 3 and Total GHG emissions
new_dr_titles: Gross scope 1, 2, 3 GHG emissions
rows.change_description: Gross scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions (with EU ETS percentage, location/market-based scope 2, significant scope 3 categories, consolidation disaggregation) are retained. The 'total GHG emissions' datapoint (44(d), 52) and the entire GHG-intensity-per-net-revenue block (paras 53-55) are removed, EU-ETS scope narrows from all regulated schemes to EU ETS only, and a separate biogenic-CO2 disclosure (para 31) is added.

old_dr_titles: GHG removals and GHG mitigation projects financed through carbon credits
new_dr_titles: GHG removals and GHG mitigation projects financed through carbon credits
rows.change_description: Same disclosure on GHG removals/storage projects, carbon credits from projects outside the value chain, and GHG-neutrality claims. Project-level detail (non-permanence management, reversals) is now required in the DR body, and the carbon-credit sub-points are streamlined (e.g. removal of EU-share and Article 6 corresponding-adjustment breakdowns).

old_dr_titles: Internal carbon pricing
new_dr_titles: Internal carbon pricing
rows.change_description: Same internal carbon pricing requirement, but streamlined from four sub-points (type, scope, prices/assumptions, covered emission volumes) to two (whether/how pricing is used in decision-making plus consistency with financial statements, and the average carbon price per scheme). DR number shifts from E1-8 to E1-10.

old_dr_titles: Anticipated financial effects from material physical and transition risks and potential climate-related opportunities
new_dr_titles: Anticipated financial effects from material physical and transition risks and material climate-related opportunities
rows.change_description: Same anticipated-financial-effects requirement covering physical/transition risks and climate opportunities. Content is realigned to IFRS S2: the acute/chronic split of physical-risk assets is removed, stranded-asset estimates are pulled into the DR body (40(a)), real-estate energy-efficiency breakdown is narrowed to loan collaterals (40(c)), and the separate reconciliation paragraph (68) is dropped in favour of a consolidated methodology disclosure (para 41).

new_dr_titles: Identification of climate-related risks and scenario analysis
rows.change_description: New 2026 DR requiring classification of each material climate-related risk as physical or transition, disclosure of the methodology for assessing exposure/sensitivity of assets to climate hazards and transition events, and details of any climate-related scenario analysis. No 2025 E1 DR carries this requirement in the topical standard; related content previously sat in ESRS 2 SBM/IRO (an unverified, out-of-scope inference not confirmed by the supplied corpus).

new_dr_titles: Resilience in relation to climate change
rows.change_description: New 2026 standalone DR on the resilience of the undertaking's strategy and business model to climate-related risks, including results of the climate resilience analysis, areas of uncertainty, and capacity to adapt. No dedicated resilience DR existed among the 2025 E1 DRs; the topic previously lived in ESRS 2 SBM-3 (an unverified, out-of-scope inference, not confirmed by the supplied E1 corpus).

old_dr_titles: Policies related to pollution
new_dr_titles: Policies related to pollution
rows.change_description: Both DRs require disclosure of pollution-related policies. The 2026 version condenses the requirement to a single reference to ESRS 2 GDR-P, deleting the objective (13), the ESRS 2 MDR-P framing (14) and the explicit sub-points (15 a–c) on air/water/soil, substances of concern, and incident avoidance. Core subject retained but the specific content the policy must address was removed.

old_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to pollution
new_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to pollution
rows.change_description: Both DRs require disclosure of key pollution-related actions and allocated resources. The 2026 version collapses the requirement into a single reference to ESRS 2 GDR-A, removing the objective (17), the ESRS 2 MDR-A framing (18) and the optional mitigation-hierarchy sub-points (19 a–c). Core requirement retained but detail removed.

old_dr_titles: Targets related to pollution
new_dr_titles: Targets related to pollution
rows.change_description: Both DRs require disclosure of pollution-related targets. The 2026 version reduces the requirement to a single reference to ESRS 2 GDR-T, deleting the objective (21), the ESRS 2 MDR-T framing (22), the explicit target areas (23 a–d), the ecological-thresholds provisions (24) and the mandatory/voluntary specification (25). Core subject retained but the prescriptive detail was removed.

old_dr_titles: Pollution of air, water and soil
new_dr_titles: Pollution of air, water and soil
rows.change_description: Both DRs cover emissions of pollutants to air, water and soil plus microplastics. The 2026 version narrows the scope to 'material' emissions identified via a managerial assessment (moving the E-PRTR Annex II list to ARs) and adds emissions due to environmental accidents; microplastics are now restricted to 'primary' microplastics manufactured/used in products, with those released into the environment reported separately. The E-PRTR consolidation/threshold rule (29) and the contextual/methodology paragraphs (30–31) were removed. Materially changed.

old_dr_titles: Substances of concern and substances of very high concern
new_dr_titles: Substances of concern and substances of very high concern
rows.change_description: Both DRs cover substances of concern (SoC) and substances of very high concern (SVHC). The 2026 version restructures the disclosure by role: manufacturers/formulators/importers of substances report weights procured/manufactured/placed on the market/released (18); users of substances report SVHC used and released (19); and manufacturers/importers/users of articles report SVHC names present above 0.1% w/w per REACH Art. 33 (20). Hazard-class split moved to ARs and limited to SVHC. Materially changed scope and structure.

old_dr_titles: Anticipated financial effects from material pollution-related risks and opportunities
rows.change_description: The 2025 DR on anticipated financial effects from pollution-related risks and opportunities has no counterpart in the 2026 revised ESRS E2, which ends at E2-5 on substances. No paragraph in new_drs corresponds to paragraphs 36–41. The deterministic hints suggest anticipated financial effects are addressed under ESRS 2 General Disclosures, but ESRS 2 is outside the supplied E1-E5 corpus, so that destination is an unverified, out-of-scope inference; the in-scope classification is that the requirement is absent from 2026 ESRS E2.

old_dr_titles: Policies related to water and marine resources
new_dr_titles: Policies related to water
rows.change_description: Both DRs require disclosure of water-related policies and both retain the provision on sites in water-stressed areas not covered by a policy. The 2026 version drops marine-resources scope, removes the detailed sub-points (water management, product/service design, consumption-reduction commitment, sustainable oceans) and streamlines the requirement to a reference to ESRS 2 GDR-P.

old_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to water and marine resources
new_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to water
rows.change_description: Both require disclosure of key water-related actions and resources allocated to their implementation, and both retain the specification of actions in areas of water stress. The 2026 version removes marine-resources scope, the mitigation-hierarchy sub-points (avoid/reduce/reclaim/restore) and points instead to ESRS 2 GDR-A.

old_dr_titles: Targets related to water and marine resources
new_dr_titles: Targets related to water
rows.change_description: Both require disclosure of water-related targets, with reference to areas of water stress. The 2026 version drops marine-resources scope, the detailed target sub-points and the ecological-thresholds provisions, reducing the requirement to a reference to ESRS 2 GDR-T with an AR on water-stress areas.

old_dr_titles: Water consumption
new_dr_titles: Water metrics
rows.change_description: Both cover quantitative water metrics for own operations (total consumption, consumption in water-stressed areas, recycled/reused, stored). The 2026 version adds total water withdrawal and total water discharge as mandatory metrics, drops 'changes in storage' and the water-intensity ratio, and moves contextual/unit guidance to ARs. Substantively the same disclosure requirement, materially expanded.
rows.divergence_note: The deterministic candidate listed E3-1, E3-3 and E3-4 as ambiguous options, but the authoritative paragraph text (water consumption/metrics for own operations) maps cleanly and solely to new E3-4 'Water metrics'; the policy and target DRs are unrelated.

old_dr_titles: Anticipated financial effects from material water and marine resources-related risks and opportunities
rows.change_description: The 2025 DR on anticipated financial effects has no counterpart among the 2026 revised E3 DRs, which contain only policies, actions, targets and water metrics. The requirement is absent from the 2026 ESRS E3 standard. (Any relocation to ESRS 2 General Disclosures is an unverified, out-of-scope inference since that text is not in the supplied E1-E5 corpus.)

old_dr_titles: Transition plan and consideration of biodiversity and ecosystems in strategy and business model
new_dr_titles: Biodiversity and ecosystems transition plan
rows.change_description: The 2025 E4-1 combined disclosure of the resilience of the strategy/business model (para. 13) with an optional transition plan (para. 15). The 2026 E4-1 drops the resilience analysis and now requires disclosure of the key features of a biodiversity and ecosystems transition plan (aligned with the GBF) where the undertaking has one and has made it public. The requirement is materially narrowed and refocused. The removed resilience content is (per non-authoritative leads) said to be handled under ESRS 2 SBM-3 — an unverified, out-of-scope inference not confirmable from the supplied E4 text.
rows.divergence_note: The deterministic candidate grouped old E4-1 with new E4-1, E4-2 and E4-4; the authoritative text shows the transition-plan subject maps cleanly to new E4-1 only, so the E4-2/E4-4 additions are unsupported.

old_dr_titles: Policies related to biodiversity and ecosystems
new_dr_titles: Policies related to biodiversity and ecosystems
rows.change_description: Same disclosure subject (biodiversity/ecosystems policies), but materially streamlined: the 2025 version's detailed sub-points (paras. 23(a)-(f) and 24(a)-(d)) are largely removed or moved into application requirements, and the 2026 version keeps only traceability of products/raw materials (13(a)) and sites in/near biodiversity-sensitive areas (13(b)), anchored to ESRS 2 GDR-P with sustainable land/ocean/deforestation practices addressed in AR 3.

old_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to biodiversity and ecosystems
new_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to biodiversity and ecosystems
rows.change_description: Same subject (actions and resources), materially simplified. The 2026 version anchors to ESRS 2 GDR-A and retains only the biodiversity-offsets disclosure (consolidating the 2025 para. 28(b) sub-points into one para. 15), dropping the mitigation-hierarchy and local/indigenous-knowledge specifications from the DR body.

old_dr_titles: Targets related to biodiversity and ecosystems
new_dr_titles: Targets related to biodiversity and ecosystems
rows.change_description: Same subject (biodiversity/ecosystems targets), materially reduced. The 2026 version anchors to ESRS 2 GDR-T and keeps only the biodiversity-offsets-in-target-setting disclosure (para. 17), removing the detailed 2025 sub-points on ecological thresholds, GBF alignment, geographical scope and mitigation-hierarchy allocation from the DR body.

old_dr_titles: Impact metrics related to biodiversity and ecosystems change
new_dr_titles: Metrics related to biodiversity and ecosystems change
rows.change_description: Retitled ("Impact metrics" -> "Metrics") and restructured. The 2026 version consolidates location-specific disclosures (locations, biodiversity-sensitive areas, and activities linked to material negative impacts) into para. 19 and requires metrics on material impacts under ESRS 2 GDR-M (para. 20), while the 2025 version's many voluntary metric sub-points (paras. 36, 38-41) are streamlined/removed.

old_dr_titles: Anticipated financial effects from material biodiversity and ecosystem-related risks and opportunities
rows.change_description: The 2025 E4-6 on anticipated financial effects has no counterpart in the 2026 E4 DRs, which end at E4-5 (Metrics). No 2026 DR in the supplied E4 corpus carries this requirement. Any relocation to ESRS 2 General Disclosures is an unverified, out-of-scope inference not confirmable from the supplied E4 text.

old_dr_titles: Policies related to resource use and circular economy
new_dr_titles: Policies related to resource use and circular economy
rows.change_description: Same DR on resource use and circular economy policies, but materially streamlined: the reference shifts from ESRS 2 MDR-P to GDR-P, the specific sub-points on transitioning from virgin resources and sustainable sourcing of renewable resources (15(a)-(b)) and the value-chain scope statement (16) are dropped, and a new requirement (para 9) to explain integration of circular economy/eco-design principles in key products is added.

old_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to resource use and circular economy
new_dr_titles: Actions and resources related to resource use and circular economy
rows.change_description: Same DR on resource use and circular economy actions, streamlined to a single sentence referencing ESRS 2 GDR-A. The optional 'may specify' list of action types (20(a)-(f)) and the objective paragraphs are removed; the core disclosure of key actions is retained.

old_dr_titles: Targets related to resource use and circular economy
new_dr_titles: Targets related to resource use and circular economy
rows.change_description: Same DR on resource use and circular economy targets, streamlined to reference ESRS 2 GDR-T. The detailed target dimensions (24(a)-(f)), waste-hierarchy layer specification (25), ecological-thresholds provisions (26) and mandatory/voluntary specification (27) are removed; the core requirement to disclose targets is retained.

old_dr_titles: Resource inflows
new_dr_titles: Resource inflows
rows.change_description: Same Resource inflows DR, but restructured around a new 'key materials' concept: it now requires a concise description of key materials, specification of critical and strategic raw materials, total weight, a per-material breakdown and secondary resources used. The prior structure (biological materials sustainably sourced, water, PP&E, methodology paragraph 32) is dropped or reframed.

old_dr_titles: Resource outflows
new_dr_titles: Resource outflows
rows.change_description: Same Resource outflows DR covering product durability/repairability/recyclability and waste. It now allows qualitative or quantitative durability/repairability disclosure, expresses waste diversion/disposal as percentages of total waste (rather than absolute weights), adds a new sub-point for waste whose final destination is unknown (16(e)), and drops the separate hazardous-waste total and waste-composition disclosures. Radioactive waste disclosure is retained.

old_dr_titles: Anticipated financial effects from material resource use and circular economy-related risks and opportunities
rows.change_description: The 2025-amended DR on anticipated financial effects has no counterpart in the 2026 revised ESRS E5, which ends at Resource outflows (E5-5). No equivalent requirement appears in the supplied 2026 E5 text. The non-authoritative hints suggest the content is addressed under ESRS 2 SBM-3, but that is an unverified, out-of-scope inference since no ESRS 2 authoritative text is in this corpus.

rows.basis: Section 2.2.2 is explicitly the 'Climate change transition plan' describing mitigation approach, 1.5°C alignment, decarbonization levers and investments; 2.2.1 provides the scenario analysis and resilience context feeding the transition plan.

Section 2.2.3 'Policies' describes climate and energy policies (Sustainability at Siemens Policy, EV100, Environmental Protection Standard); 2.2.1 lists the policies against material matters in its IRO table.
Section 2.2.5 'Actions' details decarbonization levers, building/fleet electrification and resource allocation; 2.2.2 also quantifies CapEx/OpEx investments supporting the actions.
Section 2.2.4 'Targets' sets out SBTi GHG reduction targets, energy efficiency, RE100/EV100 and CAE targets with baselines and methodology; 2.2.2 also summarizes the reduction targets.

Section 2.2.6 contains the 'Energy consumption and mix' table (total, fossil, nuclear, renewable, high climate impact intensity); 2.2.4 holds the energy efficiency target and renewable electricity commitment.
Section 2.2.6 'Metrics' reports gross Scope 1, 2 (location/market-based), Scope 3 categories, total GHG emissions and intensity ratios with methodology.
Section 2.2.6 discloses GHG removals and storage (0 tCO2e) and carbon credits cancelled/planned with project types and quality standards.
Section 2.2.6 includes the internal carbon pricing scheme table (UK, Brazil, Switzerland shadow prices/fees) and describes the approach to carbon pricing.

Section 2.2.1 covers material physical and transition risks and climate-related opportunities and resilience analysis; 1.4 states no material current financial effects were identified. Fit is partial as anticipated quantified financial effects are limited.

Section 2.3.2 is titled Policies and describes Policies on Environmental Conduct, EHS Environmental Protection Standard, DNSH Recommended Practice and Healthineers procedures governing SoCs/pollution; 2.3.1 also references these policies within the IRO overview.

Section 2.3.4 is titled Actions and details global key actions to prevent, control and reduce pollution impacts (environmental management, ODS/VOC monitoring, substance compliance, product stewardship).
Section 2.3.3 is titled Targets and sets out the voluntary 2030 target to phase out selected substances of concern in 100% of relevant products, with baseline and progress metrics.

Section 2.3.5 reports amounts of substances leaving facilities as emissions and mentions VOCs/ODS emissions; 2.3.4 covers monitoring of ODS/VOC emissions. Fit to the air/water/soil pollutant and microplastics disclosure is only partial as Siemens frames pollution mainly through SoCs.

Section 2.3.5 provides the total amounts of SoCs and SVHCs generated/used/procured and leaving facilities, directly addressing this DR; 2.3.1 and 2.3.4 describe SoC/SVHC identification and management processes.

Section 1.4 states no material current financial effects from risks/opportunities were identified and covers financial-effect statements; 2.3.1 describes pollution-related risks (regulatory changes, liabilities, costs). No dedicated anticipated financial effects quantification section exists.

Section 2.4.2 explicitly describes water-related policies (Policies on Environmental Conduct, EHS Principles and Directive, Environmental Protection Standard); 2.4.1 introduces the material IROs and lists the applicable policies.
Section 2.4.4 (Actions) details the Siemens Water Strategy, conservation program and site-specific measures with resource commitments tracked centrally.
Section 2.4.3 (Targets) states the water conservation target, baseline, target year and progress (46% to 56%).
Section 2.4.5 (Metrics) reports water consumption, withdrawal, discharge, intensity ratio and consumption in high water-stress areas.

No dedicated water financial-effects section exists; 1.4 states no material current financial effects were identified for material risks/opportunities, and 2.4.1 describes water-related risks (regulatory changes, potential liabilities/costs).

Section 2.5.1 explicitly discusses the resilience of Siemens' business model to biodiversity/ecosystem loss over short, medium and long term and how IROs originate from strategy; 1.2 covers the DMA and resilience assessment integration.

Section 2.5.2 is titled Policies and describes the EHS management system, Environmental Protection Standard, Deforestation policy and DNSH practice for biodiversity; 2.5.1 also references the policy framework.
Section 2.5.4 (Actions) describes the biodiversity conservation program, SBAT-based mitigation actions and specific site initiatives (Regensburg, Goa, Hebburn) with resources.
Section 2.5.3 (Targets) sets out the 2030 target to implement a conservation program at 100% of relevant sites with baseline and progress values.
Section 2.5.5 (Metrics) reports the number and area (0 sites, 0 hectares) of sites in or near biodiversity-sensitive areas that are negatively affected, matching the impact metrics requirement.

Section 1.4 states no material current financial effects were identified for material risks/opportunities; 2.5.1 describes biodiversity-related financial and reputational risks. Fit is partial as no explicit anticipated financial-effect quantification is given.

Section 2.6.2 is explicitly the Policies section describing EHS Principles, Environmental Protection Standard, Ecodesign and waste management policies; 2.6.1 also lists policies against material IROs.
Section 2.6.4 is the Actions section detailing Ecodesign integration, supplier training, circular business practices and waste-to-value; 2.6.1 references key actions per IRO.
Section 2.6.3 is the Targets section with RED, thermoplastics, packaging, recyclability statements and zero waste to landfill targets including baselines and progress.
Section 2.6.5 Metrics opens with Resource inflows, reporting total weight of materials, secondary content shares, critical raw materials and durability.
Section 2.6.5 also covers Resource outflows including waste generated, waste diverted/directed to disposal, recyclable content and outflow data.

No dedicated financial-effects section exists for E5; section 1.4 states no material current financial effects were identified, and 2.6.1 describes cost/risk implications of resource IROs. Fit is weak.

payload.rationale: CP1's assurance_artifact is `reconciliation_record`, the primary and decisive signal for Debate. This is the canonical Debate shape — multiple independent interpretations of one shared scope surfaced and reconciled into a single reported result, not a dependent sequential chain (Direct) and not domain-partitioned sub-results (Coalition). output_type=qualitative (a structured interpretive memo) further supports Debate. executive_summary: None of the 2026 revisions to ESRS E1-E5 remove any disclosure that Siemens can simply stop preparing; most Modified DRs are streamlined cross-references to ESRS 2, so Siemens's existing, more detailed disclosures already meet or exceed the new floor and mainly need renumbering and re-anchoring — a broadly manageable, low-effort update package.

The clearest new burdens are concentrated in Climate (E1): two brand-new disclosure requirements must be created from scratch — E1-2 (identification of climate risks and scenario analysis) and E1-3 (climate resilience) — and E1-11 (anticipated financial effects) must move from qualitative-only to quantified future effects aligned to IFRS S2, the single largest reporting-effort item in the assessment.

A small number of quantitative disclosures expand and need new data: E3-4 water metrics adds mandatory total water withdrawal and total water discharge (currently not reported); E5-4 resource inflows must be re-cut around 'key materials' with a per-material and critical/strategic breakdown; and E5-5 resource outflows must be recast to percentage-based waste reporting with a new unknown-destination category.

E2-4 (pollution to air/water/soil) is the main assurance-risk gap outside E1: it is only partially reported and materially changed, so Siemens should run the new managerial materiality assessment and cover accident emissions and primary microplastics, documenting non-materiality where the DMA supports it rather than compiling full pollutant accounting.

Every one of the four 'anticipated financial effects' DRs — E2-6, E3-5, E4-6, E5-6 — has been removed from its topical standard. The only in-scope, verified conclusion is that they are absent from 2026 E1-E5; the frequently-cited relocation to ESRS 2 is an unverified, out-of-scope inference. Because Siemens partially reported all four and the underlying risks remain material, a reporting-status review is needed before any final delete/retain/rewrite decision.

The three risk postures agree on almost everything substantive; their disagreements are mostly about whether pure-simplification rows require any action at all (minimal-change P4 often says no; balanced P5 and maximum-assurance P6 say yes) and about how urgently the removed-DR and new-DR items should be treated — see persona_divergence for the specific rows.

bullets.point: The revised ESRS this gate is comparing against does not govern FY2025. EFRAG and the Commission confirm the revised standards apply to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with early adoption only permitted for FY2026 once the delegated act enters into force. Assessing the '2026 Revised ESRS' impact on Siemens' FY2025 statement is therefore a forward-looking, hypothetical gap analysis, not a description of rules that applied to the statement being examined — the human should read every 'resulting impact' cell in that light.

search_notes: Searched EFRAG, the European Commission/EUR-Lex, ESMA and the IFRS Foundation for the current status and content of the revised ESRS. Confirmed the revised ESRS was adopted as a Commission Delegated Regulation around 3 July 2026, applies FY2027+ (early adoption FY2026), and does not govern FY2025.
Could not independently verify Siemens' FY2025 report content — that lies outside the allowed-institutions list and outside my remit; all 'reported status' claims come from the pipeline, not from me.

The most decision-relevant external facts are: (a) the revised standard does not apply to FY2025; (b) anticipated-financial-effects requirements appear relocated to ESRS 2 rather than deleted, and ESRS 2 is excluded from the corpus; (c) transitional reliefs push quantitative AFE and E2-5 SoC quantitative data to FY2030; and (d) the corpus should be checked against the final adopted 3 July 2026 delegated regulation, since ESMA and others sought changes to the draft.

bullets.point: The revised ESRS carry a phase-in that appears to soften the deliverable's single largest item: quantitative anticipated-financial-effects information (ESRS E1-11 and the ESRS 2 datapoint) is not required for financial years prior to FY2030, and quantitative substances-of-concern information prescribed by E2-5 is likewise deferred to FY2030. The deliverable rates E1-11 as required_urgent/high-effort and E2-5 as required/medium without reflecting this pre-2030 quantitative relief, so a reviewer should weigh whether the urgency and effort of the quantified AFE and SoC work are overstated for near-term reporting years.

sources.title: ESRS 1 – General Requirements | EFRAG Knowledge Hub

bullets.point: The 2026 Revised ESRS do not govern FY2025 at all. The delegated act was adopted by the Commission on 3 July 2026 and applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with early adoption for FY2026 permitted only once the act enters into force, and it becomes legally effective only after publication in the Official Journal following the scrutiny period. The deliverable frames its findings as the impact on Siemens' FY2025 Sustainability Statement; a reviewer should read this as a forward-looking gap analysis, since the earliest report Siemens could actually prepare under these rules is FY2026 (early adoption) or FY2027.

EFRAG ESRS Knowledge Hub: 2026 Revised ESRS and Voluntary Standard Interactive Document Set Now Available

bullets.point: The supervisor's own position cuts against reading the AFE reliefs as a reason to relax: in its 17 February 2026 opinion, ESMA identified the amendments to anticipated-financial-effects disclosures as a critical area of departure from ISSB standards and questioned whether the very largest, most resourceful companies (over 1,000 employees and turnover above €450m — a profile Siemens fits) should benefit from a time-limited relief on quantitative AFE. This supports the deliverable's more cautious P5/P6 stance that AFE work remains substantive even where a phase-in exists.

sources.title: Opinion of the European Securities and Markets Authority on the revised ESRS

bullets.point: The deliverable repeatedly treats the relocation of the removed 'anticipated financial effects' requirements to ESRS 2 as an unverified, out-of-scope inference — but authoritative EFRAG text confirms the substance is retained rather than eliminated. The revised ESRS E1 states that E1-11 adds topical specifications to ESRS 2 SBM-3 and that the AFE information is part of the current and anticipated financial effects required under ESRS 2 SBM-3. A reviewer weighing the four removed topical AFE DRs (E2-6, E3-5, E4-6, E5-6) should understand that the obligation most likely persists at the ESRS 2 level, so 'absent from the topical standard' does not mean 'no longer required'.

sources.title: [Draft] ESRS E1 – Climate Change (November 2025)

bullets.point: Siemens is a CSRD 'wave 1' company, and the Commission's 'quick fix' delegated act (published in the Official Journal on 10 November 2025) relieves wave 1 companies from reporting additional information for FY2025 and FY2026 beyond what they reported for FY2024, and extends phase-in provisions to all wave 1 companies. A reviewer should confirm the deliverable's FY2025 authoritative baseline actually incorporates these reliefs, as they may narrow what Siemens was obliged to report against and therefore change the real-impact reading of several rows.

sources.title: Sustainability Reporting

bullets.point: The deliverable's baseline is described as a '2025 Amended ESRS' that 'actually governed FY2025 reporting', but the text that legally governed FY2025 for wave 1 preparers is the 2023 ESRS Delegated Act (OJ 22 December 2023) as adjusted by the stop-the-clock and quick-fix measures — EFRAG's own materials note that until the amended delegated act becomes effective, in-scope companies continue to report under the 2023 ESRS. The EFRAG 'amended/simplified' ESRS produced through 2025 was draft technical advice, not law, until July 2026. A reviewer should verify which text the baseline files actually reflect so the comparison pair is authoritative on both sides.

sources.title: FAQ – The ESRS, why are revisions proposed

bullets.point: The deliverable's E1-1 reading — that the transition-plan requirement is consolidated into five key features and remains a disclose-if-you-have-one obligation — is consistent with EFRAG's public explanation that a transition plan is not mandatory, is reported only if the company has one, and consists of five key components, with companies explaining their situation where elements are missing. This externally corroborates the row's core characterization.

sources.title: EFRAG Conference 2025 – Summary report (EFRAG unveils simplified ESRS)

bullets.point: The deliverable's treatment of the new E1-2 disclosure as requiring 'details of any climate-related scenario analysis' aligns with EFRAG's stated position that scenario analysis is not mandatory but, where conducted, enables a more robust resilience assessment. This supports the row's framing that the scenario-analysis element is conditional rather than an unconditional new modelling burden.

sources.title: EFRAG Conference 2025 – Summary report (EFRAG unveils simplified ESRS)

bullets.point: EFRAG's own headline framing of the revision is a very large simplification: mandatory datapoints (to be reported if material) cut by 57%, the full set of mandatory and voluntary disclosures reduced by 68%, and the overall length of the standards shortened by over 55%. This contextualizes the deliverable's net conclusion that the changes are predominantly reductions and a broadly manageable update package, while also underscoring that the reviewer's attention is rightly directed to the handful of genuine additions rather than the bulk of the revision.

sources.title: Press release – EFRAG Shares Revised ESRS Exposure Drafts and Launches 60-Day Public Consultation

search_notes: EFRAG confirms the Revised ESRS Delegated Act was adopted by the Commission on 3 July 2026 but becomes legally effective only after Official Journal publication following the scrutiny period; as of this commentary it may still be in scrutiny, so treat the revised text as adopted-but-not-yet-in-force.

The most decision-relevant grounded finding is the ESRS 1 phase-in deferring quantitative anticipated-financial-effects (E1-11 / ESRS 2) and quantitative substances-of-concern (E2-5) information to financial years from FY2030 — this bears directly on the deliverable's top-effort items and was not visible in the gate payload.

Several E1-11 / AFE details were sourced from EFRAG Knowledge Hub 'technical advice' versions and the November 2025 draft; the finally adopted 3 July 2026 delegated-act text was not opened paragraph-by-paragraph in these searches, so exact adopted wording should be confirmed against the authoritative delegated act before sign-off.

ESRS 2 authoritative text (where the removed AFE requirements appear to relocate) was outside the deliverable's corpus; EFRAG E1 materials confirm the SBM-3 relocation, but the ESRS 2 topical wording itself was not exhaustively verified here.
